samples.summary: Held-render seam consumes the host's dirty-block set, so the render that finally paints does a full O(document) re-measure on every keystroke
samples.evidence: The wrapper calls `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` for each interior `requestRender()` while a unit is open; in the docs host that is `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531), whose last act is `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534). By the time `withUndoUnit`'s finally replays `this.requestRender()` (text-editor.ts:3847) the dirty set is gone, and `computeLayout` treats `dirtyBlockIds == null` as "cache unusable" (`canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null`, layout.ts:456-459), so every block is re-laid-out via `layoutBlock`/`measureText`. Trace of one ordinary keystroke in `handleInput` (text-editor.ts:1019-1047): `markDirty(blockId)` -> interior `requestRender()` held -> incremental relayout (dirty={blockId}) and dirty cleared -> unit closes -> replay -> full relayout of the entire document. Before this change `handleInput` produced exactly one *incremental* relayout. Every unit-wrapped action (typing, Enter, page break, paste, IME commit) now adds one whole-document re-measure, i.e. typing cost becomes proportional to document size — the same large documents issue #1045 is about. Output stays correct; only cost regresses, but it is on the hottest path and no lane measures it.

samples.summary: Hangul commit path paints an intermediate frame: the unit's replayed render runs before the caret/dirty bookkeeping that follows it, and is then repainted
samples.evidence: `applyHangulResult` wraps only `deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText()` in `withUndoUnit` (5882-5885). `deleteSelectionImpl` calls `this.requestRender()` (e.g. 4086), which is held and then replayed by `withUndoUnit`'s finally at 3845-3848 — i.e. a full paint (with `needsScrollIntoView = true` in the docs host, editor.ts:2434) happens before `markDirty(this.hangulStartPos.blockId)`, `emitComposingContext()` and `cursor.moveTo(hangulPos)` at 5907-5910, and then line 5911 paints again. So this action paints twice, the first frame showing the pre-move caret, which can produce a visible caret/scroll jump. The same double paint applies to `handleCut` (1464-1466, 1474-1476), which calls `requestRender()` after `deleteSelection()`'s unit has already replayed one. This also contradicts the "held and replayed once — at most once" claim in `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment (3822-3823), which is per-unit, not per-action.

verdict.reason: The described mechanism exists exactly as claimed — I verified it end to end: the held-render wrapper calls requestLayoutRefresh (text-editor.ts:733-742), the host wires that to recomputeLayout (editor.ts:2531), which clears dirtyBlockIds after use (editor.ts:1526-1534), and the replayed requestRender in withUndoUnit's finally (text-editor.ts:3843-3849) reaches renderWithScroll -> render -> recomputeLayout (editor.ts:2434-2438, 2208-2211) with dirtyBlockIds undefined, so canUseCache is false (layout.ts:456-459) and every block takes the layoutBlock branch (layout.ts:535-538). However, this is refuted as out-of-scope for the Correctness lens: it produces no wrong behavior of any kind — the reviewer concedes "Output stays correct; only cost regresses". The final layout, pagination and paint are byte-identical to pre-change; there is no wrong condition, boundary error, null/undefined crash, async/ordering mistake, swallowed error, leaked resource, or inconsistent state. Nothing in the lane's severity tiers (data loss, crash, wrong result on a reachable path, inconsistent state for the next step) applies. The cost claim is also overstated, which removes the "breaks a core flow" reading: typing was already document-proportional before this change — computeLayout builds a fresh LayoutBlock for every block on every pass even on cache hits (layout.ts:468-562, per its own comment at 471-481), computeTableLayout re-runs for every table irrespective of the cache (layout.ts:506-530), and paginateLayout walks every block on every pass (pagination.ts:75); canvas measurement of unchanged runs is memoised per (measurer, font, text) in computeCharOffsets (layout.ts:585-602), so the extra pass is not a fresh measureText sweep but a constant-factor addition to an already O(document) pass. That is a performance finding for a perf/blast-radius lens, not a blocking correctness defect.
